title.narrative: Emergency Agricultural Food Aid to Vulnerable Households and Farmers in the West Bank

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project, led by ACF with MAA'N, will sustain household (HH) food access and protect local food production in the most affected areas of the West Bank (WB). The intervention directly contributes to the FSS Outputs 1.1 and 1.2, 2025 Flash Appeal, and aligns with the oPt HF 2025 Fourth Reserve Allocation. The project responds to a dual food security crisis. In Bedouin communities in the Eastern Slopes livelihoods face systematic threat due to destruction of agricultural assets, restricted access to grazing land and water, and shortages of inputs. In parallel communities in northern WB experience recurrent displacement and severe HH food insecurity. To address these needs, the project combines emergency food assistance with targeted agricultural and livelihoods support, prioritizing vulnerable HHs and farmers.ltbrgtACF and MAA'N will support vulnerable farmers and herders through distribution of production inputs and materials, using conditional cash where needed, across Hebron, Bethlehem, Jerusalem, and Ramallah (ACF), and Tubas governorates (MAA'N). Assistance will include animal fodder and supplies, irrigation equipment, and reinforcement and protection of animal shelters from settler’s attacks and theft through provision of steel fencing and doors to mitigate settler attacks, and shelter covers to protect livestock from violence and poor weather conditions. A total of 80 animal shelters will be reinforced or protected in Wad Salman (Ramallah), and in At Twaneh, Um Faggara and Ar-Rakeez (Hebron). In addition, 110 animal shelter covers will be provided to vulnerable herders in Abu Shusheh Bedouin community (Jerusalem), and in Al-Walayda and Arab Al-Rashayda–Al-Barriya (Bethlehem).ltbrgtIn Tubas governorate, 74 herders in Al-Hadidya, Samra, Ein Al-Hilwah, Al-Farsiya (Ilhmayer and Nabe Al-Ghzal), Al Aqabeh, Mak-hul, and Al-Himma will receive essential production inputs and equipment to mitigate the impact of ongoing settler violence and military restrictions (fodder and veterinary kits). 46 greenhouses in Bardala and Ain Al-Baida will also be supported with materials such as pipes and plastic sheets to repair and protect productive infrastructure. Emergency food assistance will be provided through e-vouchers to 670 HHs (320 HHs in Jenin and 350 HH in Tulkarm refugee camps) over 3 rounds. Targeting will prioritize female-headed HHs, HHs with no income, HHs of more than 5, and HHs including children, elderly persons, and persons with disabilities. In coordination with the relevant stakeholders (WFP, UNRWA, FSS team), each HH will receive an e-voucher valued at USD 82 (ILS 250) per round (equivalent to USD 16.5/ILS 50 per individual), sufficient to meet basic food needs and reduce reliance on negative coping strategies. ACF will also coordinate with PAR to ensure complementarity and avoid duplication. ACF will lead voucher distribution in Tulkarm camps, while MAA'N will lead in Jenin refugee camp with joint monitoring, verification, and reporting.ltbrgtThe project will benefit 980 HHs (310 through agricultural/livelihood support and 670 through e-voucher assistance), corresponding to an estimated 4,974 individuals (1320 women, 1370 men, 1119 girls, 1165 boys). The intervention has been designed in close coordination with FSS partners, UNRWA, the MoSD, the MoA, local authorities, and local committees to ensure complementarity, avoid duplications, and smooth execution. ACF and MAA'N bring experience in similar interventions, ensuring effective targeting and operational feasibility. The expected outcomes include the restoration and protection of local food production systems, immediate life-saving support for vulnerable HHs, and strengthened HH resilience. The project will be implemented in line with humanitarian principles, with safeguarding, inclusion of PWDs and elderly, gender mainstreaming, environmental approaches, and accountability to populations ensured through community participation and feedback and complaint mechanisms.ltbrgtlt/pgt
